About us

MoEVing is India's only Electric Mobility focused Technology Platform with a vision to accelerate EV adoption in India. With an integrated approach to demand aggregation, supply optimization, connecting with charging infrastructure and financing, it aims to onboard 1 million EV by 2030, have 50% of India’s charging stations on its app, finance large proportion of EV fleet and facilitate financing of the same through other partners, and abate 5 Billion MT of carbon. Our differentiator is credible people with 50+ years of experience in managing electric fleet operations, cutting edge technology to drive operational efficiency and comfortable working in the B2B space. Want to be part of creating a better work? Explore open positions at MoEVing here: https://moeving.freshteam.com/jobs

Delhi’s EV Policy 2026 marks a defining moment for commercial electric mobility in India.

Having been closely associated with Delhi’s EV journey over the years, it’s encouraging to see the government build on that foundation with an even stronger focus on commercial fleet electrification.

The policy introduces a phased transition that will see all new L5 three-wheelers and N1 goods carriers move to electric from January 1, 2027, alongside enhanced incentives and a ₹15,000 crore commitment to accelerate EV adoption.

With a stronger focus on charging infrastructure and commercial fleet electrification, this roadmap positions Delhi to become one of the world’s leading cities for electric mobility. For the commercial EV ecosystem, this marks the beginning of the next phase of growth.

This comes as right moment where India is dealing with West Asia crisis and energy security is of paramount importance for the country. 

#ElectricMobility #DelhiEVPolicy #CommercialEVs #SustainableLogistics #MoEVing

Vikash Mishra

Today I spoke at the Smart Freight Week 2026 in Amsterdam on unlocking financial pathways for zero-emission trucks in India.
After years of operating in this space, I believe this: the technology is ready, the corporate demand is real, and the economics of electric freight already work. What hasn't kept pace is the financing.
The biggest barrier isn't upfront cost — it's how lenders value the asset. Residual value uncertainty keeps EV truck loans expensive and short. And batteries with 70–80% remaining capacity at end of first life have real second-life value that current financing models ignore.
What the sector needs is: loan terms aligned to actual payback timelines, Priority Sector Lending classification for EV trucks under RBI, and first-loss default guarantee from development finance institutions.
The next chapter of Indian logistics will be electric. Financing will determine how fast.
A big thank you to Smart Freight Centre for convening what was one of the most meaningful roundtables I've been part of — the right institutions, the right questions, and a real appetite to create an impact. Grateful to fellow panelists from IFC, EBRD, BloombergNEF, Kabisa, UC Davis, and DST.

Kartik D. James Falzon Nicholas Hu Jacob Teter Nikolaos Soulopoulos Nina Zhao Christoph Wolff Pramod Rajendran Naidu Sanya Shahi Satish Kedar Nath 
#ElectricTrucks #ZeroEmissionFreight #MoEVing #EVFinancing #SmartFreightWeek #GreenFreight

On 30th March, I spoke at Women Who Move the Nation: From Parliament to Highways — a dialogue with Rajya Sabha MPs on gender, freight, and clean mobility organised by Swaniti Initiative, Purpose , and Nayi Soch Ki Sawaari at the Constitutional Club of India.

My session was on EV trucks as an opportunity for women in transport — as drivers, operators, and entrepreneurs. At MoEVing, we have deployed women EV drivers in last-mile logistics. The barrier has never been capability. It’s access.

What made this event meaningful was the room itself — women truck drivers, fleet operators, and Rajya Sabha MPs in one conversation, engaging seriously on what gender empowerment in freight looks like on the ground.

Glad to have been part of it.

Saudamini Zutshi Harsimran Kaur  
#WomenInTransport #CleanMobility #EVs #WomenWhoMoveTheNation #MoEVing #GreenFreight

• How India’s ZET financing gap can be bridged through blended finance, leasing, and risk-sharing
